lead.headline: Israel's election ends in deadlock: Likud is the largest party, but neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's has a majority
lead.short: With more than half the ballots counted, The Times of Israel projected Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc to win 56 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's alliance 49, both short of the 61 needed. Television projections gave Likud about 27 seats to 21 for Eisenkot's Yashar party. Netanyahu said the "true results" were a day or two away, and called for a right-wing government.

why.text: Netanyahu wants a free hand to restart the war on Iran, and a deadlock leaves that decision hanging over oil prices.

more: Speaking at Likud headquarters in West Jerusalem after polls closed on Tuesday, Netanyahu said Israel could not rely on coalitions with Arab parties "that are against our existence". He listed Hamas, Hezbollah and Iranian leaders killed during his term and said Israel had a "historical opportunity" with Donald Trump "to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all".

Arab parties are on track for a record number of seats, polls show. Alon Pinkas, a former Israeli diplomat, said whichever side leads may need an uncomfortable coalition deal, though opposition voters would not want one with Netanyahu. Trump claimed credit for Netanyahu's showing, saying "the whole tide turned".

facts.projection: Netanyahu bloc 56, Eisenkot bloc 49 (Times of Israel)

update.new: The vote is in: no bloc has a majority, and Likud is the largest party.
update.front: The result is a deadlock, with weeks of coalition bargaining ahead.

seconds.headline: Abhishek Sharma hits 113 off 38 balls and India chase 199 in 13.2 overs to win the T20I series in Wellington
seconds.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · CRICBUZZ · 28 OCT
seconds.short: India beat New Zealand by six wickets in Wellington to take an unbeatable 3-0 series lead. Chasing 199, Abhishek Sharma made 113 off 38 balls and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, made 45 off 19. India got there in 13.2 overs, reaching 118 without loss in the powerplay, the highest score in the first six overs of a men's T20I.

why.text: India have won the series with two games to spare, and found an opening pair that scares every attack.

more: India reached 50 in 2.2 overs, equalling the joint-fastest team fifty in the format, and passed 100 inside five. Abhishek said Sooryavanshi had promised in the nets to bat like the hero of Bhaag Milkha Bhaag: "Bhaiya, khelunga bhi waise hi" (Brother, I will play the same way). "Special mention to Vaibhav," Abhishek said.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar, back after four years, has one wicket in three games. "I did not chase this, though it was always the dream," he said, adding that he would keep playing domestic cricket. The fourth T20I is in Auckland on Friday, and India play the Hong Kong Sixes the same day.

facts.result: India won by six wickets, chasing 199 in 13.2 overs

update.new: India won the third game by six wickets and the series 3-0 with two to play.
update.front: India have won the series, with a record powerplay.

seconds.headline: The US tells Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the midterms, officials say
seconds.byline: HINDUSTAN TIMES · THE WALL STREET JOURNAL · 28 OCT
seconds.short: The US has told several Gulf countries to be ready for a short, intense military campaign against Iran after the 3 November midterms, people briefed on the talks said. It is moving a Patriot battery from Texas and restocking munitions, and an extra carrier group is due next month. Trump has not decided, but is leaning towards a large attack.

why.text: A renewed war would hit Gulf oil and the Indians working there, and Brent is already above $110.

more: Targets could include Iranian infrastructure and nuclear sites, people familiar with Trump's thinking said. The alternative is a deal; regional mediators are still trying. The White House said it would not comment on "sensitive military plans that may or may not exist", and that Trump "keeps all options on the table to ensure that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon".

Israel has also prepared targets, and Netanyahu has pushed for strikes to resume. Trump has said he will not attack before the midterms. On Tuesday the Houthis said they hit Saudi Arabia's biggest oil refinery, a 550,000 barrel-a-day plant, and Brent rose more than 1% on Wednesday.

facts.moves: Patriot battery from Texas, extra carrier group next month
facts.refinery hit: 550,000 barrels a day, per the Houthis

update.new: The US is warning Gulf states of a post-midterm campaign.
update.front: Washington is now telling its allies to get ready, the clearest sign yet that the war may resume.

seconds.headline: Rahul Gandhi says the Tata Group is 'being criminally destroyed' and asks why business leaders are silent
seconds.short: "Tata is being criminally destroyed, and no business leader dares say a word. How long will you stay silent? Until they own you?" Rahul Gandhi wrote on Wednesday, saying "Indian business is not Modi and Shah's plaything". It is the first time the Congress has spoken on the fight over Tata Sons' leadership, which has split its trustees.

why.text: The fight decides who controls India's biggest conglomerate, and it is now a political battle as well as a boardroom one.

more: Earlier this week Noel Tata, chairman of Tata Trusts, challenged the resolution reappointing N. Chandrasekaran as chairman of Tata Sons, passed at the board meeting on 17 September. Tata Trusts, which owns 66% of Tata Sons, calls the reappointment illegal because Noel Tata vetoed it. Gandhi said the Congress "will ensure justice for these crimes".

A proposed restructuring would take Tata Sons out of the RBI's framework for core investment companies, which would otherwise require it to list. The RBI governor, Sanjay Malhotra, said last week that upper-layer finance companies must list. Whether the change works depends on its final structure and the RBI's view, lawyers say.

update.new: The Congress joins the Tata fight; Noel Tata challenges Chandrasekaran's reappointment.
update.front: The country's biggest business fight has become a political one.

seconds.headline: Anthropic's filing shows Amazon, not the venture funds, stands to gain most from its listing, with notes Amazon values at $97.9bn
seconds.short: None of Anthropic's venture backers owns 5% of the company, its filing shows, because at a private valuation of $965bn even large bets are small slices. Amazon is likely the biggest winner: it holds convertible notes with $6.2bn in principal, which its own filings valued at $97.9bn on 30 June, and could convert into up to 1.84 billion shares.

why.text: It shows how much of the AI boom's gains flow to the cloud giants that supply the computing.

more: Menlo Ventures' roughly $14bn position is only about 1.5% of the company, Bloomberg figures suggest. Amazon first backed Anthropic in 2023 with up to $4bn and structured much of its later money as notes that turn into shares at a listing. A cap limits Amazon to 12% of Anthropic's partially diluted shares.

As the notes rose in value, Anthropic had to book the difference as a cost: $72.4bn in the first half of 2026, a non-cash charge that explains much of its reported loss. The notes are Anthropic's entire debt. Its seven founders have tightened their control ahead of the listing, other reports say.

update.new: Who owns what: Amazon's notes and the founders' control.
update.front: The filing shows for the first time who gets rich from the biggest AI listing, and it is Amazon.

stories.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro flies to the US after missing a deadline to hand in his passports, and Washington says it will give his family visas
stories.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · REUTERS · 28 OCT
stories.short: Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election to Lula, has left Brazil for the US after failing to surrender his passports within 24 hours, as the Supreme Court had ordered in a money-laundering inquiry. His passports were then cancelled. He is reportedly in Miami with his wife and two daughters, and a US official said they would get visas.

why.text: It turns a lost election into a diplomatic quarrel between Lula and Trump, a week after Lula told Washington Brazil is nobody's backyard.

more: Lula, speaking in Brasília, called the departure shameful and said Bolsonaro should have stayed to prove his innocence. A senior federal police official said Bolsonaro had not left through any regular border point. On Monday he had denied any plan to flee, saying he would surrender his passports and defend himself.

Bolsonaro has not formally conceded, though his Liberal Party acknowledged Lula's win on Monday. Trump, a close ally of his father Jair Bolsonaro, said on Monday the vote "looked like another rigged election", without evidence. Lula has accused the US of colluding with the Bolsonaros to return the family to power.

facts.US: visas for him and his family

update.new: Bolsonaro has fled to the US; his passports are cancelled.

stories.headline: Two Britons are charged over an alleged Iran-linked plot at RAF Fairford, the US-run base in England
stories.short: Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, was charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, which police believe to be Iran's, and Nouman Essghir, also 24, with entering a prohibited place on 22 August for a purpose prejudicial to the UK. Both appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday. Three suspicious vans had been found near the base on 27 September.

why.text: It is the first criminal case in Britain to tie Iran to a plot against a base the US uses in its war on Iran.

more: The vans, bearing the logo "Fuel2You", came across a Ministry of Defence Police cordon and changed route; no explosives were found, but petrol was seized. Five men were arrested, and police later said one of them had called 999 to report what was happening. Dozens of residents were evacuated.

Essghir's charge relates to an alleged "reconnaissance mission" a month before the incident. He was remanded in custody, and Abdulkarim was bailed on condition he surrenders his passport. A 25-year-old British-Iranian arrested on suspicion of helping a foreign intelligence service was released without charge. The case moves to the Old Bailey on 20 November.

stories.headline: Mbappé apologises after calling Mao a 'Chinese dictator', as three Chinese brands drop him
stories.short: Kylian Mbappé apologised on Tuesday after a video showed him describing a meme of his face on Mao Zedong's body as "a guy... I think he was a Chinese dictator". "My comment was ill-judged," he said. Drinks maker Dongpeng, dairy group Mengniu and cheese maker Milkground ended their deals with him, and China's state broadcaster wants a formal apology.

why.text: Madrid's biggest star has a commercial problem in one of football's largest markets, two days after winning the Clásico.

more: "I apologize to everyone my words have upset. This was absolutely not my intention. I have deep respect for the Chinese people and their history, and I am sincerely sorry," Mbappé said. The clip was filmed before his appearance on the French online talk show The Bridge.

China's foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said words that hurt the feelings of Chinese people "will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society". The social media platform RedNote said its partnership with Mbappé had already ended, and blocked his account from gaining new followers. Fans online often joke that Mbappé is a dictator because of his larger-than-life presence.
